The promotion of certain beliefs some North Carolina lawmakers have likened to “critical race theory" is on track to be banned in state government workplaces, under a bill that received final legislative approval on Tuesday, June 6, 2023. (AP Photo/Gerry Broome, File) By Joe Bruno, wsoctv.com November 16, 2026 at 3:43 pm EST RALEIGH, N.C. — North Carolina lawmakers are heading back to Raleigh this week with several major issues still unresolved, including four bills awaiting potential veto overrides.
 Among them are a bill dealing with open carry and another that would shorten the state’s early voting period.
 ALSO READ: Charlotte City Council declines to override Mayor Rob Harrington’s veto Lawmakers will also have to address the gas tax. The current repeal is set to expire at the end of November, putting the issue back on the legislative agenda.
 The session comes during the final months of the Republican Party’s near-supermajority in the General Assembly. When the new legislature is sworn in next January, Democrats are set to take control of the North Carolina House.
